questions.question: How is data organized in ServiceNow?

explanation.correct: In ServiceNow, data is organized in a database with tables, records, fields, and values. Tables store records, records contain fields, fields hold individual pieces of data, and values are accessed through fields and records. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: ServiceNow uses a relational database structure, not a file system.
These are spreadsheet concepts, not ServiceNow's data structure.
While ServiceNow uses object-oriented concepts, data is stored in tables.

source.excerpt: In ServiceNow, data is organized in a database with tables, records, fields, and values.

questions.question: What is a sys_id in ServiceNow?

options.text: A unique 32-character ID that identifies each record

explanation.correct: Records have a unique 32-character ID called a sys_id. This identifier is automatically generated and uniquely identifies each record in the database. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: User login names are stored in the user_name field, not sys_id.
Table names are separate from record identifiers.
Field labels are display names, not unique record identifiers.

source.excerpt: Records have a unique 32-character ID called a sys_id.

questions.question: In ServiceNow table extension terminology, what is a base class?

options.text: A parent class that is not an extension of another table
Any table that has at least one child class
A table created by an administrator with the u_ prefix
The table with the most records in the instance

explanation.correct: A table that extends another table is a child class, and the table it extends is the parent class. A parent class that isn't an extension of another table is a base class, such as Task [task] or Configuration Item [cmdb_ci]. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-extension-and-classes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A table with children is a parent class, but it's only a base class if it doesn't extend anything itself.
The u_ prefix marks a custom global table; it has nothing to do with base classes.
Record count doesn't define a base class.

source.excerpt: A parent class that is not an extension of another table is called a base class.

questions.question: When can administrators extend a table from another table?

options.text: At any time by editing the Extends table field
Only after the table has records

explanation.correct: Table extension lets child tables share fields and records with a parent table. Administrators and application developers can only extend tables during table creation. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-extension-and-classes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The extends relationship can't be added to an existing table later.
Records aren't required, and extension must happen at creation.
Dictionary overrides change field behavior on child tables; they don't create extensions.

source.excerpt: Administrators and application developers can only extend tables during table creation.

questions.question: Which tools can administrators use to see the relationships between table classes? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: Administrators can use the schema map, the system dictionary, and the Tables module to see the relationships between classes. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-extension-and-classes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Update set preview checks for update set conflicts.
Transform maps define import field mappings.

source.excerpt: Schema map … System dictionary … Tables module

questions.question: Which of these are required system fields added automatically to every table? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: Required system fields added to all tables include Class [sys_class_name], Created [sys_created_on], Created by, Sys_id [sys_id], Updates [sys_mod_count], Updated by, and Updated [sys_updated_on]. You can't delete or modify them. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/r_GlobalDefaultFields.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: sys_domain_path relates to domain separation and isn't in the list of required system fields.
u_ fields are custom fields that administrators create.

source.excerpt: Sys_id [sys_id] … Created [sys_created_on] … Updates [sys_mod_count]

questions.question: What does the Updates [sys_mod_count] system field store?

options.text: The number of updates to the record since it was created
The number of users watching the record
The number of update sets containing the record

explanation.correct: Updates [sys_mod_count] is an integer field that counts the number of updates to a record since it was created. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/r_GlobalDefaultFields.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Watchers are stored in a watch list field.
sys_mod_count isn't related to update sets.
Child records aren't counted in this field.

source.excerpt: A numeric field that counts the number of updates for this record since record creation.

questions.question: An administrator wants the Priority field to default to 5 on Incident, without changing its default on Task or Change. What should they configure?

options.text: A dictionary override on the Incident table
A change to the dictionary entry on the Task table
A client script on the Task table
A new Priority field on the Incident table

explanation.correct: Dictionary overrides let a field on an extended table be defined differently from the parent table field. For example, an override can change a Task field's default value on Incident without affecting Task or Change. Overridable aspects include reference qualifiers, attributes, default values, calculations, dependencies, display values, and mandatory and read-only status. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DictionaryOverrides.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Changing the Task dictionary entry would affect all child tables.
A client script on Task is not the tool for per-table field defaults.
Duplicate fields cause confusion and don't override the inherited field.

source.excerpt: Dictionary overrides provide the ability to define a field on an extended table differently from the field on the parent table.

questions.question: Which aspects of an inherited field can a dictionary override change? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: Administrators can override reference qualifiers, dictionary attributes, default values, calculations, field dependencies, default column display values, and mandatory and read-only status. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_DictionaryOverrides.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The column name isn't in the list of overridable aspects.
The data type isn't in the list of overridable aspects.

source.excerpt: Reference qualifiers … Default values … Mandatory and read-only status

questions.question: An administrator creates a custom table named Laptops in the global application. What prefix does the system add to the table name?

explanation.correct: For a table in the global application, the name is prefixed with u_. Tables in a scoped application get a namespace identifier prefix. The prefix can't be modified. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/t_CreateATable.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Scoped tables get a namespace identifier; x_ is typical for custom scoped apps, but global tables use u_.
sys_ is used for system tables.
sn_ is used by ServiceNow-provided scoped apps.

source.excerpt: For a table in the global application, the name is prefixed with the string u_.

questions.question: The Watch list field on Incident lets users select multiple User records. What kind of field is it?

explanation.correct: Glide lists let a user select multiple records on the table the glide list defines, such as the Watch list field on Incident selecting records from sys_user. Reference fields select one record. Document ID fields can point to a record on any table. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-relationships.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: A reference field selects a single record, like the Caller field.
Document ID fields point to a record on any table.
Many-to-many relationships are shown as related lists, not as a single field.

source.excerpt: the Watch list field on the Incident [incident] table allows the user to select records on the User [sys_user] table.

questions.question: How can two tables be joined virtually so you can report on data stored in more than one table?

explanation.correct: Two tables can be joined virtually in a database view to enable reporting on data stored across more than one table. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-relationships.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dictionary overrides change how an inherited field behaves.
UI policies change form behavior.
Transform maps move data from import sets to target tables.

source.excerpt: Two tables can be joined virtually in a database view to enable reporting on data that might be stored over more than one table.

questions.question: Which table stores custom many-to-many relationship definitions?

explanation.correct: The Many to Many Definitions [sys_m2m] table lets administrators create custom many-to-many relationships. Many-to-many tables don't count toward your custom table allotment. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/t_CreateAManyToManyRelationship.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: sys_dictionary stores table and column definitions.
This is not where many-to-many definitions are created in this procedure.
cmdb_rel_ci stores relationships between CIs.

source.excerpt: The Many to Many Definitions [sys_m2m] table allows administrators to create custom many-to-many relationships.

questions.question: In the schema map, which color shows tables that the selected table extends (Extending)?

explanation.correct: Schema map colors: Referenced by is red, Referencing is orange, Extended by is green, and Extending is blue. The selected table is shown in yellow. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_SchemaMapForTables.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Green shows Extended by.
Red shows Referenced by.
Orange shows Referencing.

source.excerpt: |Extending|Blue|

questions.question: Why does ServiceNow warn administrators to be careful when changing system dictionary entries? (Choose two.)

options.text: Dictionary changes automatically apply to all extended tables unless a dictionary override is defined
Changes to sys_ tables can cause system-wide issues, such as not being able to use update sets
Dictionary changes are only saved in the user's session
Dictionary changes delete all records in the table

explanation.correct: Dictionary changes are difficult to reverse and apply to all extended tables unless a dictionary override is defined. Changes to system tables (starting with sys_) can cause system-wide issues, such as not being able to use update sets. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_SystemDictionary.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dictionary changes are persistent and system-wide.
Changing a dictionary entry doesn't delete records.

source.excerpt: dictionary changes automatically apply to all extended tables unless a dictionary override is defined … can create system-wide issues such as the inability to use update sets

questions.question: What is the role of the import set table in the import process?

options.text: It is a staging area for records imported from a data source before they are transformed
It is the final destination table for imported records
It stores user preferences for imports

explanation.correct: The import set table is a staging area for imported records. A transform map then defines how fields in the import set table relate to fields in the target table. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetsKeyConcepts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The target table is the destination; the import set table is only staging.
Transform map scripts are stored with the transform map.
User preferences aren't stored in import set tables.

source.excerpt: The import sets table acts as a staging area for records imported from a data source.

questions.question: An administrator needs another column in an import set table. What is the recommended approach?

options.text: Add the column to the input data, then use Test Load 20 Records or Load All Records to generate it
Add the column manually to the import set table in the dictionary
Add the column to the transform map only
Create a dictionary override on the import set table

explanation.correct: Import set table columns are generated automatically and shouldn't be added manually, because that can affect scheduled cleanup and leave orphaned records. Add the column to the input data and reload to generate it. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetsKeyConcepts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Manually adding columns is specifically discouraged.
Transform maps map existing columns; they don't create import set columns.
Dictionary overrides don't create columns.

source.excerpt: first add the column to the input data, then select Test Load 20 Records or Load All Records to auto generate the columns in the import set table.

questions.question: What does a data source record define in System Import Sets?

options.text: Where to get the data to import, such as a file, a JDBC database, or an LDAP organizational unit
How import set fields map to target fields
Which users can view the imported records
When a transform map is deleted

explanation.correct: A data source defines where to get the data to import. Types include File, JDBC, LDAP, OIDC, REST (Integration Hub), Data Stream, and Custom (Load by Script). See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetsKeyConcepts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Field mapping is defined by transform maps.
Access is controlled by ACLs.
Data sources don't manage transform map lifecycles.

source.excerpt: A data source may point to a file, a JDBC-compatible database, or an LDAP organizational unit.

questions.question: A transform map for user imports has Coalesce selected on the Email field map. During transformation an import row's email matches an existing user record. What happens?

options.text: The existing user record is updated
A duplicate user record is created
The row is skipped with an error
All users with that email are deleted

explanation.correct: With coalesce, the instance checks for an existing target record with the same value in the coalesce field. If it finds one, it updates that record. If not, it creates a new record. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetCoalesce.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Coalesce prevents duplicates by updating matching records.
A match updates the record; it doesn't cause an error.
Coalesce never deletes records.

source.excerpt: If an existing record with a matching value in the target table is found, that record is updated.

questions.question: What happens during a transform if no coalesce field is defined on the transform map?

options.text: All imported rows are treated as new records and no existing records are updated
Existing records with matching sys_ids are updated
Only the first row is imported

explanation.correct: If no coalesce is defined, all imported rows are treated as new records and no existing records are updated. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetCoalesce.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Without coalesce, no matching is done.
The transform still runs; it just inserts.
All rows are processed.

source.excerpt: If no coalesce is defined, all imported rows are treated as new records.

questions.question: A transform map coalesces on both First name and Last name. When is an existing target record updated?

options.text: Only when all coalesce field values match
Always, for the most recently updated record

explanation.correct: With multiple-field coalesce, all coalesce field values between the target and staging tables must match for the target record to be updated. For OR-style matching, use a conditional coalesce script. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetCoalesce.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Either-field matching needs a conditional coalesce script.
A non-match inserts a new record.
Updates depend on matching coalesce values.

source.excerpt: All coalesce field values between the target and staging tables must match to coalesce with multiple fields.

questions.question: Why should you coalesce only on fields with unique values?

options.text: If more than one target record matches, only the first matching record is updated
Non-unique fields can't be used in field maps
The import fails if duplicates exist
Coalesce fields are automatically made unique

explanation.correct: Choose coalesce fields only if they have unique values. If more than one record in the target table matches, only the first matching record is updated. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetCoalesce.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Any field can be mapped; uniqueness matters for correct matching.
The import doesn't fail; it updates the first match.
Coalesce doesn't change field uniqueness.

source.excerpt: If more than one record in the target table matches the specified coalesce options, only the first matching record in the target table is updated.

questions.question: In a transform map, which transformation event script runs at the start of an import run, before any data rows are read?

explanation.correct: The onStart event script runs at the start of an import run, before any data rows are read. onBefore and onAfter run for each row, and onComplete runs at the end. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/r_MapWithTransformationEventScripts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: onBefore runs before each row is transformed.
onAfter runs after each row is transformed.
onComplete runs at the end of the transform.

source.excerpt: The onStart event script is processed at the start of an import run, before any data rows are read.

questions.question: By default, what does the scheduled Import Set Deleter job delete?

options.text: Import sets and their related import set rows created more than seven days ago
All target table records created by imports
Transform maps that haven't been used in seven days

explanation.correct: The Import Set Deleter under System Import Sets > Import Set Tables > Scheduled Cleanup deletes import sets and their related import set rows created more than seven days ago by default. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/delete-import-sets.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Target table records aren't deleted by the cleanup job.
Transform maps aren't deleted.
Data sources aren't deleted by this job.

source.excerpt: Defaults to deleting import sets and their related import set rows that were created more than seven days ago.

questions.question: Which user do import sets run as, and what limitation does this cause?

options.text: They run as user System and can't add data to encrypted fields
They run as the logged-in user and can't import more than 20 rows
They run as admin and bypass all data validation
They run as guest and can't write to task tables

explanation.correct: Import sets run as user System and therefore can't add data to encrypted fields. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetsKeyConcepts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Import sets don't run as the logged-in user; 20 rows is only the Test Load option.
This is not how import sets are documented.
Import sets don't run as guest.

source.excerpt: Import sets run as user System and therefore cannot add data to encrypted fields.

questions.question: Which table stores the basic attributes of all IT configuration items?

explanation.correct: The core Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] class stores the basic attributes of all CIs, and its descending classes are IT CIs. The CI Relationship [cmdb_rel_ci] class defines relationships between CIs, and the Base Configuration Item [cmdb] class is the core table for non-IT CIs. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_ConfigurationManagementDatabase.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: cmdb_rel_ci stores relationships, not CI attributes.
Task is the base for work records such as incidents.
Assets are tracked in asset tables; this question is about CI attributes.

source.excerpt: The core Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] class, which stores the basic attributes of all the CIs.

questions.question: In the CMDB relationship [Server1] [Managed by] [Server2], which is the parent CI?

options.text: Neither; CMDB relationships have no parent

explanation.correct: A CMDB relationship consists of a parent CI, a child CI, and a relationship type. In [Server1] [Managed by] [Server2], Server1 is the child, Server2 is the parent, and Managed by is the relationship type. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_CIRelationships.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Server1 is the child CI in this example.
Managed by is the relationship type.
Every CMDB relationship has a parent and a child.

source.excerpt: Server2 is the parent CI

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the CMDB Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE)?

options.text: To provide a central framework for identifying and reconciling CI data from different sources, preventing duplicate CIs
To create reports on incident volumes

explanation.correct: Identification and Reconciliation provides a central framework for identifying and reconciling data from different sources. It helps keep the CMDB accurate when multiple data sources create and update CI records, and can also be applied to Import Sets to prevent duplicate CIs. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_CMDBIdentifyandReconcile.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Incident reporting is done with reports and dashboards.
Discovery schedules are configured in Discovery.
IRE doesn't encrypt data.

source.excerpt: The Identification and Reconciliation module provides a centralized framework for identifying and reconciling data from different data sources.

questions.question: Which health indicators does CMDB Health evaluate and aggregate into health scores? (Choose three.)

options.text: Number of open incidents per user

explanation.correct: Health indicators such as duplicate CIs, required CI fields, and audits are evaluated and aggregated into health scores at the class, health group, and service levels. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_CMDBHealth.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Incidents per user is not a CMDB health indicator.
Update set conflicts aren't CMDB health indicators.

source.excerpt: Health indicators such as duplicate CIs, required CI fields, and audits are evaluated and aggregated into health scores

questions.question: What is the Common Service Data Model (CSDM)?

options.text: The data model standard for all products that use the CMDB, with guidelines for where CIs and relationships belong
A reporting dashboard for incident trends

explanation.correct: The CSDM is the data model admins should follow when they set up ServiceNow products. Its standards for defining CIs and relationships make sure data lives in the right CMDB tables. The CSDM is the data model standard for all products that use the CMDB. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-landing-page.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: CSDM is a data model, not a dashboard.
CSDM guides how the CMDB is used; it doesn't replace it.
CSDM isn't a security framework.

source.excerpt: The CSDM is the data model standard for all products that use the Configuration Management Database (CMDB).

questions.question: Which CSDM domain contains base referential data, such as business processes and contracts, that the other domains reference?

explanation.correct: Tables in the Foundation domain hold base data that objects in the other CSDM domains reference. Foundation tables aren't used in CMDB relationships; they hold critical referential data. You must populate foundational data before using ServiceNow products. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/foundation-domain.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Service Consumption holds the catalog of service and business offerings.
Build & Integration holds data for building or integrating what was designed.
Ideation & Strategy holds ideas and concepts.

documentation.section: Foundation domain in the CSDM model

source.excerpt: Tables in the Foundation domain contain base data that is referenced from or to objects in the other CSDM domains.

questions.question: In the CSDM, what are the three base service types?

explanation.correct: ServiceNow provides three base service types in the CSDM: Business, Technical, and Application. You can extend them to match the service types your organization uses. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-term-definitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: These are CI categories, not CSDM service types.
These are ITSM processes.
These are change types.

source.excerpt: ServiceNow provides three base service types: … Business … Technical … Application

questions.question: According to the CSDM terms, how are assets and CIs related?

options.text: Many, but not all, assets are CIs, and many, but not all, CIs are assets
Every asset is a CI and every CI is an asset
Assets and CIs are never the same item
Assets are a child class of CIs

explanation.correct: An asset is an item whose financial value is tracked. The CSDM terms note that many, but not all, assets are CIs, and many, but not all, CIs are assets. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/common-service-data-model-csdm/csdm-term-definitions.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The CSDM definitions state the overlap is partial.
Assets and CIs often overlap.
The relationship is overlap, not a class hierarchy.

source.excerpt: Many, but not all, assets are CIs and many, but not all, CIs are assets.

questions.question: Which CMDB class is the core table for non-IT configuration items?

explanation.correct: The Base Configuration Item [cmdb] class is the core CMDB table for non-IT CIs; its descending classes are non-IT CIs. The Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] class stores the basic attributes of all IT CIs. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_ConfigurationManagementDatabase.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: cmdb_ci is the core class for IT CIs.
cmdb_rel_ci defines relationships between CIs.
Computer is an IT CI class that extends cmdb_ci.

source.excerpt: The Base Configuration Item [cmdb] class, which is the core CMDB table for non IT CIs

questions.question: How can relationships between CIs get into the CMDB? (Choose two.)

options.text: Many relationships can be loaded automatically through Discovery
An administrator can create or edit relationships from the CI form, for example with the CI relationship editor
Relationships are only created by importing a spreadsheet
Relationships are created automatically whenever an incident is opened

explanation.correct: CI relationships can be discovered automatically; with Discovery, many relationships are loaded during the discovery process. You can also add, create, or edit relationships from the CI form with the CI relationship editor, or with Unified Map in CMDB Workspace. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/c_CIRelationships.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Imports are one source, but not the only one.
Opening an incident doesn't create CI relationships.

source.excerpt: If you use Discovery, many relationships can be automatically loaded into the system through the discovery process. … by launching the CI relationship editor from the CI form

questions.question: Which table extension models does the ServiceNow AI Platform offer? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: The platform offers three extension models: table per class, table per hierarchy, and table per partition. The model determines how many database tables are created, how fields are derived from parent classes, and how records are replicated from child classes. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-extension-and-classes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Table per field is not an extension model.
Table per scope is not an extension model.

source.excerpt: Table per class … Table per hierarchy … Table per partition

questions.question: What does the Class [sys_class_name] system field indicate on an extensible table?

options.text: Which child table contains the record
The CSS class used to render the form
The user role required to read the record
The application scope of the table

explanation.correct: On an extensible table, Class [sys_class_name] is a field that indicates which child table contains the record. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/r_GlobalDefaultFields.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: It has nothing to do with CSS styling.
Roles are set in ACLs, not in this field.
Scope isn't stored in sys_class_name.

source.excerpt: If the table is extensible, a string field that indicates which child table contains the record.

questions.question: An incident import sets the Caller field, and the import ends up updating the sys_user table. What is this called?

explanation.correct: A foreign record insert happens when an import changes a table that isn't the import's target table. It happens when a reference field is updated; for example, setting the caller on an incident actually updates the sys_user table. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetsKeyConcepts.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Coalesce matches rows to existing target records; this isn't a collision.
Nothing is rolled back here.
onComplete is a transform script event that runs at the end of an import.

source.excerpt: when updating a value for the caller on an incident, the import is actually updating the sys_user table.

questions.question: What does a reference field store in ServiceNow?

options.text: The full content of the referenced record
The unique sys_id of a record from another table
A copy of the referenced table
The URL of an external system

explanation.correct: A reference field stores the unique sys_id of a record from another table, creating a link between them. This link makes fields from the reference table accessible in the form. Reference fields only connect to one table. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Reference fields store the sys_id, not the full record content.
Tables are not copied; only a reference link is created.
External URLs are stored differently; reference fields link internal records.

source.excerpt: A reference field stores the unique sys_id of a record from another table, creating a link between them.

questions.question: What happens when a table extends another table in ServiceNow?

options.text: The child table inherits all fields from its parent table along with its unique fields
The parent table can no longer be used

explanation.correct: An extended table inherits all fields from its parent table along with its unique fields. When extending a table, all fields and properties from the parent table are inherited, while unique fields can be added to the child table. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: The parent table remains intact; extension creates a relationship.
Child tables have additional unique fields beyond inherited ones.
Parent tables remain fully functional after extension.

source.excerpt: An extended table inherits all fields from its parent table along with its unique fields.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of tables that extend the Task table?

explanation.correct: Examples of parent tables in ServiceNow include the Task and Configuration Item tables, which are extended to create child classes like change, request, incident, and problem. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: User and Group are separate tables, not extensions of Task.
Location and Department are reference tables, not Task extensions.
Knowledge tables extend different parent tables.

source.excerpt: Examples of parent tables in ServiceNow include the Task and Configuration Item tables, which are extended to create child classes, like change, request, incident, and problem.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Schema Map in ServiceNow?

explanation.correct: The Schema Map visualizes table relationships. You can use the schema map to identify which columns originate on a table and which columns are inherited from parent tables, plus what tables are referenced. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: User permissions are managed in the security modules, not schema map.
System performance is tracked with different tools.
Notifications are managed in System Notification modules.

source.excerpt: Schema map visualizes table relationships.

questions.question: What is the difference between a field name and a field label?

options.text: Field names are unique and may differ from labels, which are display names
Field labels are used in scripts; field names are for display

explanation.correct: Field names are unique and may differ from labels. For instance, 'city' is the field name in the sys_user table for the label 'Location'. Labels are display names shown to users. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Field names and labels often differ, as shown with city/Location example.
It's the opposite - field names are used in scripts, labels are for display.
There is a clear difference between technical names and display labels.

source.excerpt: Field names are unique and may differ from labels. For instance, city is the field name in the sys_user table for the label Location.

questions.question: What is a Document ID field used for?

options.text: To reference one record from any table

explanation.correct: Document ID fields allow selecting one record from any table, unlike reference fields which only connect to one specific table. Example: Document field in the Translated Text table. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Attachments are stored differently, not through Document ID fields.
PDF exports are handled by reporting functions.
Version history is tracked separately.

source.excerpt: Document ID fields allows selecting one record from any table. Example, Document field in the Translated Text table.

questions.question: Which of the following are types of field relationships in ServiceNow? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: ServiceNow supports one-to-many relationships (using reference fields like Caller on Incident linking to User) and many-to-many relationships (connecting two or more tables so related records are visible in both, like students and classes). See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/australia/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-relationships.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: One-to-one-to-many is not a standard relationship type in ServiceNow.
Circular reference is not a defined relationship type in ServiceNow's data model.

source.excerpt: You can create relationships between tables by extending tables, referencing records in another table, creating many-to-many relationships, and joining tables in a database view.
